s1.syndrome_frame: Acute chest pain with exertion, associated with ischemic changes on cardiac testing
salient_findings: Substernal chest pain triggered by running more than 2 miles
ST depressions during recovery phase of exercise treadmill test
Severe ischemia in the distribution of the left anterior descending and circumflex arteries on PET-MPI
key_facts: Substernal chest pain lasting less than 5 minutes
Chest pain occurs with running more than 2 miles
Hypertension controlled with lisinopril and hydrochlorothiazide
No family history of premature coronary artery disease
No chest pain during exercise treadmill test
ST depressions during recovery phase of exercise treadmill test

shortlist.label: Stable Angina
shortlist.why_kept: Chest pain with exertion and ischemic changes on cardiac testing

shortlist.label: Unstable Angina
shortlist.why_kept: Recent onset of chest pain with exertion and evidence of ischemia on PET-MPI

shortlist.label: Acute Coronary Syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Evidence of ischemia on PET-MPI and ST depressions during recovery phase of exercise treadmill test

shortlist.label: Myocardial Infarction
shortlist.why_kept: Severe ischemia in the distribution of the left anterior descending and circumflex arteries on PET-MPI

shortlist.label: Variant Angina
shortlist.why_kept: Chest pain with exertion and evidence of coronary artery spasm

shortlist.label: Coronary Artery Spasm
shortlist.why_kept: ST depressions during recovery phase of exercise treadmill test and evidence of ischemia on PET-MPI

shortlist.label: Cardiac Syndrome X
shortlist.why_kept: Chest pain with exertion and evidence of ischemia on cardiac testing without significant coronary artery disease

shortlist.label: Familial Hypercholesterolemia
shortlist.why_kept: High LDL level and family history of hypertension

raw.rationale: The patient's symptoms of substernal chest pain triggered by physical exertion (running more than 2 miles) and relieved by rest, along with evidence of ischemia on PET-MPI and 3-vessel involvement on CCTA, are characteristic of stable angina. The lack of chest pain during the exercise treadmill test but presence of ST depressions during recovery also supports this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Unstable Angina
rejected.why: The patient's symptoms are predictable and triggered by exertion, which is more typical of stable angina. Unstable angina is characterized by a change in the pattern or severity of chest pain.

rejected.label: Acute Coronary Syndrome
rejected.why: There is no indication of acute myocardial infarction or other features of acute coronary syndrome in the vignette.

rejected.label: Myocardial Infarction
rejected.why: The patient does not have evidence of myocardial necrosis, which is required for the diagnosis of myocardial infarction.

rejected.label: Variant Angina
rejected.why: The patient's symptoms are not consistent with variant angina, which typically occurs at rest and is caused by coronary artery spasm.

rejected.label: Coronary Artery Spasm
rejected.why: While coronary artery spasm could cause chest pain, the patient's symptoms and test results are more consistent with stable angina due to atherosclerotic disease.

rejected.label: Cardiac Syndrome X
rejected.why: The patient has evidence of significant coronary artery disease on CCTA and coronary angiogram, which is not typical of cardiac syndrome X.

rejected.label: Familial Hypercholesterolemia
rejected.why: The patient's LDL level is elevated, but there is no indication of a familial pattern of hypercholesterolemia or other features of this condition.
